Regenerated 2026-09-26 on branch feat/phase10-14-complete. Previous value recall@10 0.825 / mrr 0.6322. The gate had been failing before this regeneration; it was not caused by the changes made alongside it, and that was established by bisecting the corpus rather than assumed:
  corpus @ d80ffb6 (where 0.825 was recorded)  -> recall@10 0.850  PASS
  corpus @ e8ed971 (pre-session HEAD)          -> recall@10 0.725  FAIL by 0.100
  current code on that same e8ed971 corpus      -> recall@10 0.725, mrr 0.4336
  corpus @ HEAD plus this session's files       -> recall@10 0.700  FAIL by 0.125
The third line is the load-bearing one: the current code reproduces the old code's numbers exactly (0.725 / 0.4336) on an unchanged corpus, so the code changes in this session have no effect on retrieval at all. The whole 0.850 -> 0.700 slide is corpus drift: the golden queries are about ai_db/ source, but the eval root is '.', so every new test file and benchmark script added since d80ffb6 competes with the code in the BM25 index. No golden entry was edited -- eval/golden/ai_db.jsonl has not changed since d80ffb6.
eval/results/ is now in .aidbignore so generated benchmark artifacts (token_budget.json alone is 63 KB of JSON containing the words 'latency', 'percentiles' and 'telemetry') stay out of the search space. That fix plus the .aidbignore trailing-slash bug are real corrections; neither recovers the 0.850, because the remaining drift is legitimate new source.
This number guards code regressions from here. If it moves again, check the corpus before suspecting the code.
